We hope FairStress gives researchers a way to uncover hidden asymmetries in model decision-making, test fixes, & develop more consistent systems.
📝 Blog: allenai.org/blog/fairstress
📄 Paper: allenai.org/papers/fairstr…

signals.name: Ai2
signals.text: Since LLMs have various biases in their decisions and reasoning, we then examined how training data might influence this, & find that LLMs are never really taught fair decision-making yet are often aligned to prevent discrimination—which may explain over-correction patterns.

signals.name: Ai2
signals.text:
We tested 9 approaches for reducing these gaps. Most didn’t reliably improve symmetric robustness; some hurt performance.
Older benchmarks like BBQ can miss overcorrection, but FairStress reveals the hidden asymmetries they overlook.

We’re training it on observed-weather & +4°C datasets, adding outputs like temperature, snow, & ice + exploring ways to make HiROv2 10×+ faster.

signals.name: Ai2
signals.text:
Together, ACE + HiROv2 can generate years of global climate data at resolutions fine enough to capture storms, severe winds, & other local extreme events.
And it’s cheap: global 3 km simulations cost ~300× less than X-SHiELD, with even bigger savings for individual regions.

signals.name: Ai2
signals.text:
HiROv2 is especially strong on extremes: it matches the distribution of extreme events in X-SHiELD to within 3% for 1-in-a-million rain, wind, & pressure predictions.
It also captures cyclone energy, realistic hurricanes, & strong downslope winds.
Demo: ace.allen.ai

signals.name: Ai2

Tracking salmon by analyzing video helps researchers monitor their populations. But when a salmon-tracking system makes a mistake, like an overcount, fixing it can mean editing clips frame after frame by hand.
What if you could just tell the system to fix what it got wrong?
